title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
abstract: arXiv:2611.16088v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods. tldr: 本研究首次将在通用合成表格数据上预训练的基础模型TabPFN应用于稀疏CPT数据的地下土层概化，无需岩土领域微调或预设层边界即可重建二维土层剖面，其精度在合成剖面上接近SchemaGAN，并在实际场地数据上优于SchemaGAN和参考插值方法。
en_tdlr: This study applies TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, to subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data—reconstructing 2D soil profiles without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries—achieving mean errors close to SchemaGAN on synthetic sections and lower errors at both field sites in the Netherlands.
